generated_at: Nov 23, 2026, 10:25 AM ET (markets open; figures are from Monday morning and will change through the day)
tldr: Stocks bounced back hard Monday morning after the worst week in years, with the S&P 500 up about 4.6% and the TSX up about 2.5%.
Nvidia led the rebound after its board brought back Jensen Huang as CEO, lifting chipmakers and other AI stocks.
Wall Street’s fear gauge has calmed down but is still high, and U.S. markets close Thursday for Thanksgiving.

market_pulse.note: Up about 4.6% Monday morning near 7,228, bouncing back after seven straight losing days that ended Friday at 6,910.39 (Yahoo Finance).
market_pulse.detail: The S&P 500 tracks 500 of the biggest U.S. companies, so it is the best single snapshot of the U.S. market. Last week it fell 8.6%, its worst week since April 2025, so today's jump only wins back part of that drop.

market_pulse.note: Up roughly 6.5% to 7% Monday morning, the biggest gain of the major indexes, after a 5.28% drop Friday to 22,617.73 (Yahoo Finance; JournalArta).
market_pulse.detail: The Nasdaq is packed with technology companies, so it swings the most when big tech stocks move. Most of today's gain is coming from chipmakers and AI-related companies.

market_pulse.note: Up more than 1,200 points, close to 3%, Monday morning after Friday's close of 48,147.33 capped its worst week since 2020 (Yahoo Finance).
market_pulse.detail: The Dow follows 30 large, well-known U.S. companies. It is rising less than the Nasdaq today because it holds fewer of the tech stocks leading the rebound.

market_pulse.note: Up about 2.5% at Monday's open, following Wall Street higher (JournalArta).
market_pulse.detail: Canada's main index leans more on banks, energy and mining than on tech, which is why it usually moves less than the Nasdaq on days led by U.S. tech stocks. U.S. markets close Thursday for Thanksgiving while the TSX stays open.

themes.title: Nvidia jumps after Jensen Huang is reinstated as CEO
themes.summary: Nvidia shares rose more than 30% Monday morning after its board unanimously reinstated co-founder Jensen Huang as CEO, effective immediately. The stock opened at $167.04, about 27% above Friday's close (Yahoo Finance; The Hill; CNBC).
themes.detail: Nvidia makes the chips that power most AI systems, and it is one of the largest companies in the world, so its moves pull the whole market. Even after today's jump, the stock is still well below where it was in October.

themes.title: Relief rally after the worst week in years
themes.summary: All three major U.S. indexes are sharply higher after last week's selloff, when the S&P 500 fell 8.6% and the Nasdaq dropped about 10% (Yahoo Finance).
themes.detail: After very steep drops, markets often have strong bounce days as some buyers step back in. One strong day does not by itself mean the slide is over, which is why many outlets are calling this a relief rally.

themes.title: Chipmakers and AI stocks lead the rebound
themes.summary: Intel rose about 13% to 14%, AMD about 6% to 7% and Oracle about 13%, while cloud-computing firms CoreWeave and Nebius jumped as much as 30% (Yahoo Finance; City A.M.).
themes.detail: Many companies depend on Nvidia's chips or sell to the same AI customers, so good news for Nvidia tends to lift the whole group. These same stocks led last week's drop.

themes.title: Fear gauge eases but stays high
themes.summary: The VIX, Wall Street's measure of expected volatility, fell about 25% to roughly 26.8 at the open, though it remains in a range associated with nervous markets (JournalArta; 24/7 Wall St.).
themes.detail: The VIX rises when investors expect big price swings. A falling VIX means fear is cooling, but a reading in the mid-20s still signals more uncertainty than usual.

themes.title: Short holiday week
themes.summary: U.S. markets are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving and close early at 1:00 PM ET Friday; Canada's TSX keeps normal hours (NYSE).
themes.detail: Holiday weeks often have fewer traders, which can make moves bigger than usual. Several major economic reports are being squeezed into Wednesday before the break.

sectors.name: Technology
sectors.note: Leading the market Monday, driven by Nvidia and other chipmakers, after being the weakest sector last week (Yahoo Finance; CNBC).
sectors.detail: Technology is the biggest part of the U.S. market by value, so when it moves, the indexes follow. Today's leadership is a reversal of last week's heavy selling.

sectors.name: Semiconductors
sectors.note: Chip stocks are rebounding sharply: Nvidia up about 30%, Intel up about 13% to 14% and AMD up about 6% to 7% (Yahoo Finance; City A.M.).
sectors.detail: Semiconductors are the chips inside everything from phones to AI data centres. They tend to swing more than the overall market in both directions.

sectors.name: AI cloud providers
sectors.note: CoreWeave and Nebius jumped as much as 30% after Huang's return (Yahoo Finance).
sectors.detail: These companies rent out computing power built on Nvidia chips. Their shares often move with Nvidia because their businesses depend on it.

sectors.name: Energy
sectors.note: Oil prices are lower Monday, which is weighing on energy shares relative to tech (JournalArta).
sectors.detail: Energy companies earn more when oil prices are high, so falling oil usually holds them back. This matters for Canada, where energy is a large part of the TSX.

watch_list.why: October PCE inflation, the second estimate of third-quarter GDP, durable goods orders and jobless claims are all due Wednesday, Nov. 25 at 8:30 AM ET (JournalArta; Schwab).
watch_list.detail: PCE is the inflation measure the U.S. Federal Reserve watches most closely. Hotter-than-expected numbers could change expectations for interest rates, which affects both stocks and borrowing costs.

watch_list.why: Monday's jump follows seven straight losing days; outlets note the VIX is still elevated heading into a short, data-heavy week (24/7 Wall St.; Yahoo Finance).
watch_list.detail: Big bounce days are common during sharp selloffs. How stocks behave over the next few sessions will say more than any single day.

watch_list.why: The Bank of Canada announces its rate decision at 9:45 AM ET and the U.S. Federal Reserve at 2:00 PM ET on Wednesday, Dec. 9 (Bank of Canada; Federal Reserve).
watch_list.detail: These decisions set the base for mortgage, loan and savings rates. Markets often move in the days leading up to them as expectations shift.
